title: Polynomial-time input-fragment production
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with a binary code for its optional states, and let $t$ be a time function whose unary encoding is polynomial-time computable. Then the function that maps each Boolean word $z$ to the input fragment for $M$ at time $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: the unary encoding of $t(z)$ is polynomial-time computable
replaced: For every source machine, state code, and polynomial-time unary time producer, the serialized input fragment at the produced time is polynomial-time computable; both template choices are finite protected tables, and the branch predicate and shifted variable address are charged.
